reviews.review: Remake of Indie Classic Risk of Rain

There are so many signs that this game had endless amounts of love and care put into it. This isn't something that was made as a product, it was made with passion.

[h1]And man does it make me immensely sad that I just didn't enjoy my time with Risk of Rain Returns.[/h1]

As someone with over 700 hours in Risk of Rain 2, I was excited to try a 2D version of that. I had never played RoR1, so I couldn't tell you how this compares, but to RoR2… well it's just… worse. I understand the disservice that I'm doing by comparing this to that, but the highs of RoR2 were so high that this just feels like a massive let-down.

The controlls feel incredibly stiff and slow. It felt like a bad retro platformer in the way characters awkwardly snap in their movement with no momentum and tiny, stilted jump height. Your default movement speed is aggregiously slow when compared to the size of the maps you'll be traversing, and some characters don't even get a fun movement option. Even of the ones that do, they're not nearly as satisfying as something like Loader's Spider-Man grappling hooks or Mercenary's dashes. Instead, everyone feels the exact same, just with a minor dash or blink here or there. No crazy map-spanning leaps or teleports, just you and your light jog with barely anything to do to speed up the clunky traversal through awkwardly laid out levels that I struggled to navigate even a dozen hours in.

The pacing feels a lot worse too. It feels like you get fewer items, they have less of an impact, and you get them slower when compared to the incredible pacing of RoR2. Even on a "god run," where I felt I had picked up all the greatest items, I still never felt as powerful or dazzled as I would in other roguelikes when you "break" the game. In fact, just from a visuals standpoint, everything is so tiny on the screen that it feels like you're watching an action scene but from miles away.

Even with a faster move speed, higher jump, and other movement perks that feel like they should've been the baseline, I struggled to find the teleporter, the end goal of each level, to advance to the next stage almost every run. This was never an issue in RoR2, where you could easily spot particle effects after just a few seconds of traversing the map, allowing you to more easily plan your route through the stage. A minimap of any kind would've been great for visualizing the stages and helping you plan routes through the shockingly vertical levels, connected by launchers that seem to cause more damage from falling that enemies, and ropes that never felt good to climb up and down over and over.

All the animations, sound effects, music, and particle effects are gorgeous and perfectly executed. When you're just using the moves against one enemy that's directly in front of you and they're not moving, and you're just experiencing the basic functionality of the game, it feels great, and that sucks. I can tell there's a really fun game underneath this that doesn't feel like I'm just button mashing all my moves instead of making interesting positioning decisions and tactically deciding when to activate all my abilities when more enemies fill up the screen. I tried it on my PC. I tried it on my TV. I tried it on my Steam Deck. Different control schemes, custom control layouts. Macros. I really, really tried to make this game work for me and it just refused to cooperate.

So much of this game I love. I kept leaving every session thinking how bad the game felt, but then picking the game back up because everything around the gameplay was phenomenal. Hopoo can do some amazing things, but I think the gameplay here missed the mark for me. However, I don't think everyone will feel the same way I did, and I can easily see others enjoying this experience, and the game has a ton of content for those looking for something that can give them hundreds of hours of things to do, but ultimately I think I've put down the game for the last time and don't have any plans to give it another shot again.
